findings.body: Removing `escapeHtml` and passing `body` straight into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` turns every comment into an HTML/JS injection sink. A body like `` or `` executes in the reader’s origin. Restore escaping for plain text, or parse a limited markdown subset and render through React elements / a vetted sanitizer (e.g. DOMPurify with a strict allowlist) before any HTML sink. Do not assign raw user/community content to `__html`.

summary: ## Verdict Critical XSS regression — do not merge until comment HTML is sanitized again. ## Narrative `Comment` previously escaped `&`, `<`, and `>` before passing the string into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, which made the DOM sink safe for plain text. verification.reason: The patch removes escapeHtml and assigns the raw body prop to dangerouslySetInnerHTML, creating a clear XSS sink for comment content. Base still escaped HTML entities before the same sink, so this is a real regression at critical severity.
